en: to be smart; to be bright

examples.en: That child is young but really bright.
A sharp junior joined, so I feel reassured.
It was a child with bright-looking eyes.
I'm raising a smart-looking puppy.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 똘똘해서 말을 빨리 배웠어요.
examples.en: My daughter is bright and learned to talk early.
Class is fun thanks to a bright student.

explain: 주로 어린아이나 젊은 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 아랫사람을 보는 느낌이 들 수 있어서 '똑똑하다'가 더 안전해요. '똑똑하다'보다 야무지고 귀여운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: A bright child lives next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 어린아이를 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often praises a child by modifying a noun.

phrases.example: 그 학생은 눈이 반짝여서 똘똘해 보여요.
phrases.en: That student looks bright with sparkling eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 느끼는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression based on looks.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게도 쓸 수 있는 더 안전한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A safer word that can be used for adults too.

explain_en: It is mainly used to praise children or young people. Used on an adult it can sound condescending, so '똑똑하다' is safer. It feels more sharp-and-cute than '똑똑하다'.

examples.en: Talking loudly on the phone in a movie theater is really rude and thoughtless.

examples.ko: 줄을 서지 않고 새치기하는 건 몰상식한 행동이에요.
examples.en: Cutting in line is senseless, rude behavior.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말이 너무 몰상식해서 대화하기 싫어요.
examples.en: He speaks so rudely that I don't want to talk to him.

examples.ko: 몰상식하게 쓰레기를 길에 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't throw trash on the street so thoughtlessly.
I was careful because I didn't want to be called rude.

examples.ko: 어른께 그렇게 말하는 건 좀 몰상식하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it a bit out of line to speak to an elder like that?

explain: 예의나 기본 상식이 없는 행동을 비난할 때 써서 꽤 강한 말이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하기보다 행동을 두고 '몰상식한 행동'처럼 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '예의가 없다', '개념이 없다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A person with no common sense upset me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 없는 사람을 비난할 때 쓰지만 강한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a rude person, but it's a strong expression.

phrases.en: I saw someone behaving without any common sense on the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 행동을 꾸밀 때 써요. 비난하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게 it describes how someone acts; it carries strong criticism.

phrases.en: Talking loudly on the phone in a theater shows no sense.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday alternative to 몰상식하다.

explain_en: It criticizes behavior that lacks basic manners or sense, so it is quite strong. People usually use it about an action, as in '몰상식한 행동', rather than say it directly to a person. In daily talk Koreans also say '예의가 없다' or '개념이 없다'.

examples.en: The defendant entered the court with his lawyer.
The defense counsel argued for innocence.

examples.ko: 경찰은 조사 전에 변호인을 부를 수 있다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The police said he could call counsel before questioning.
The defense side submitted new evidence.

examples.ko: 그는 믿을 만한 변호인을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is looking for a trustworthy lawyer.
I heard the defense counsel's statement on the news.

explain: 재판이나 수사에서 피고인 편에서 돕는 사람을 가리켜요. 일반적으로 법률 일을 하는 직업은 '변호사'라고 해요. 같은 사람이어도 사건 안에서의 역할을 말하면 '변호인', 직업을 말하면 '변호사'예요.

phrases.en: The defense side said the evidence was not enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판 뉴스에서 피고인 쪽 사람들을 함께 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in trial news for the defendant's side as a whole.

phrases.en: A famous defense team took the case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명이 함께 변호하는 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A team of several people defending together.

phrases.en: I want to become a lawyer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건 안의 역할이 아니라 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the profession rather than the role in a case.

explain_en: It refers to the person who stands with the accused during a trial or investigation. The profession is 변호사. The same person is 변호인 when you talk about the role in a case, and 변호사 when you talk about the job.

examples.en: It's really thoughtless of you to say that.
Thoughtless behavior makes things hard for everyone.
You're not a child, so why are you so thoughtless?
Everyone was shocked by his indiscreet words.
I apologize for my thoughtless behavior.
You end up regretting careless spending later.

explain: 앞뒤를 가리지 못하고 경솔하다는 뜻이라 사람이나 행동을 비판할 때 써요. '철없다'는 어린 느낌이 강하고, '분별없다'는 어른에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대는 '분별 있다'이고, 주로 '분별없는 행동/말'로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 분별없는 말 때문에 친구가 상처를 받았어요.
phrases.en: My friend was hurt by thoughtless words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각 없이 한 말을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize words said without thinking.

phrases.en: If you act recklessly, you will regret it later.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form '분별없이' placed before a verb.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 분별없지 않아요. 늘 신중해요.
phrases.en: He is not indiscreet. He is always careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 신중하다는 뜻을 전할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can convey that someone is careful.

explain_en: It means being careless without thinking things through, so it is used to criticize a person or an action. '철없다' feels childish, while '분별없다' can be used for adults too. The opposite is '분별 있다', and it is mostly used as '분별없는 행동/말'.

en: to be upright; to be square; to be right-minded

examples.ko: 그분은 마음이 올곧아서 거짓말을 못 해요.
examples.en: He is so upright that he can't tell a lie.

examples.ko: 올곧은 성격 때문에 손해를 볼 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I lose out because of my upright character.
My teacher is someone who has lived an upright life.
He stayed upright against every temptation.

examples.ko: 올곧다는 평가를 받는 기자가 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: A reporter known as upright received an award.
I want to be an upright and warm person.

explain: 주로 사람의 마음, 태도, 삶이 바르고 곧을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. 활용은 '올곧아요, 올곧은, 올곧게'처럼 해요.

phrases.en: He is an upright person, so everyone trusts him.
Our teacher is very upright at heart.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for giving praise.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived an upright life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶의 태도를 말할 때 부사형 '올곧게'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form 올곧게 describes how one lives.

explain_en: It is mostly praise for a person's mind, attitude or way of life being right and straight. It conjugates as '올곧아요, 올곧은, 올곧게'.

examples.ko: 그 아저씨는 입심이 좋아서 늘 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That man is a great talker, so he's always popular.

examples.ko: 입심 좋은 사회자 덕분에 행사가 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the smooth-talking host, the event was fun.
Nobody can beat my grandmother's gift of gab.
Some broadcasters make a living with their way with words.

examples.ko: 그 가이드는 입심도 좋고 아는 것도 많아요.
examples.en: That guide talks well and also knows a lot.

examples.ko: 입심만 믿고 준비 없이 발표하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't present without preparing, relying only on your talking skills.

explain: 보통 '입심이 좋다', '입심이 세다'처럼 말해요. '입담', '말솜씨'와 비슷하게 쓰이는 구어적인 말이고, 말을 막힘없이 잘한다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 입심이 세서 아무도 못 이겨요.
phrases.en: Grandma is so quick-tongued that nobody can beat her in talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 지지 않고 막힘없이 잘한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of never losing in a verbal exchange and talking without pause.

phrases.example: 그는 입심 좋게 이야기를 풀어 갔어요.
phrases.en: He told the story with great fluency.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb describing the way someone speaks.
phrases.en_equiv: fluently; with a gift of gab

phrases.en: He's a good talker, so his stories are always fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입심과 비슷하지만 이야기를 재미있게 한다는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 입심, but with more emphasis on telling entertaining stories.

explain_en: It is usually said as '입심이 좋다' or '입심이 세다'. It is a colloquial word used much like '입담' or '말솜씨', and it suggests speaking fluently without hesitation.
